A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CEA heuristic-learning work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J are readable and support comparison, including matching material across reflow and figure renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original Rubik’s Cube experiments comparing CEA, cross-entropy training, and compressed PDBs, together with model-size experiments and overestimation distributions in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds an empirical generalization-error analysis in Figure 2 and a qualitative finding from testing 8-bit inference.

M1.justification: The CEA loss, delta heuristic, ResNet architecture, and staged beta/eta tuning remain unchanged. The added sampling description documents implementation details. Training in 32-bit precision and inference in 16-bit precision were already specified in v1 Appendix G.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 8-corner, 6-edge, 7-edge, and delta(6,4)-edge Rubik’s Cube PDBs, with the same 4-edge base PDB. The additional sample-size and precision analyses do not introduce new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain neural networks trained with CE and PDBs using min compression. Their participation in Table 2 is unchanged; the added compression references do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation of generalization error versus training-instance count and reports an 8-bit quantized-inference trial. Existing experimental settings in Table 4 remain unchanged. The newly described sampling procedure does not establish a change to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds a sample-size sensitivity analysis for generalization error and a brief precision experiment reporting accuracy loss at 8 bits. The existing model-size analysis, overestimation distributions, and beta/eta tuning plots are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these experiments. The new generalization-error curve has no uncertainty reporting; the retained appendix box plots describe prediction distributions rather than variability across runs.

E6.justification: Figure 2 newly reports decreasing generalization error as training-instance count increases, and Section 5 adds the qualitative 8-bit accuracy-loss finding. V2 also cites Futuhi and Sturtevant (2025) for generating fewer than half as many search nodes as a size-matched compressed PDB; this is an attributed result. Tables 1–5 and the existing appendix plots retain their values.

T1.justification: V2 restricts the consistency definition explicitly to graph edges and corrects |G_V| = n² to |G_V| ≤ n². Section 3.1 spells out conditions for the cited inconsistency bound, some already discussed in Appendix E. The principal theorem bounds and Appendix D–F proofs retain their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: CEA-based heuristic learning, near-admissible Rubik’s Cube heuristics, tighter sample-complexity bounds, and generalization guarantees for goal-dependent heuristics.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new curve as confirming the predicted 1/sqrt(N) decay. It also explains training over the full PDB as information compression and identifies accuracy loss as the reason for rejecting 8-bit inference. These add interpretations and a practical limitation.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly describes uniform sampling within heuristic classes, allocation proportional to class size, and sampling from the full dataset for a fixed number of epochs. Hardware, hyperparameter tables, state encodings, and PDB access information remain unchanged. The 32-bit/16-bit precision disclosure moves from Appendix G to the main text.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Futuhi and Sturtevant (2025), Han et al. (2015), Micikevicius et al. (2017), and Krishnamoorthi (2018). It explicitly acknowledges that Theorem 1 matches Sakaue and Oki’s bound despite a different derivation. Appendix A’s related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: V2 adds short passages on sampling, precision, and generalization error, expands several background explanations, and makes local wording and notation corrections. The main section order and Appendices A–J remain intact, with most existing prose unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds the generalization-error plot as Figure 2. Existing Figures 2–8 become Figures 3–9 with their graphics preserved. Tables retain their structure, while surrounding text and displays reflow and conference-publication headers are added.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves transparency through sampling documentation, limited mathematical corrections, and clearer attribution of the existing bound. The new generalization analysis and disclosed failed 8-bit trial add useful evidence. However, Figure 2 lacks a clear error-estimation protocol and uncertainty reporting, limiting its claimed confirmation of the theoretical rate. The core results and appendix proofs remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
